description: Replace the n2048 reducer's 372-launch direct-panel and GPU-wide baddbmm sequence with a device-resident multi-cluster progression: form exact wider panels, execute tensor-core symmetric trailing updates inside the extension, advance panel epochs without host dispatch, and retain reflector ownership, eigensolve/backtransform, certificates, fallbacks, all smaller-size routes, and CUDA guards; profile launch, reducer, and update phases.

Collapsed the n2048 host loop of 186 width-11 cluster panels plus 186 ATen baddbmm updates into one eight-CTA resident cluster per matrix. Exact panel formation and reflector ownership remain; rank-local live factors feed four-term TF32 WMMA for the first eight columns, with strict scalar completion for columns 8-10 and partial tiles. Build and kernelguard pass; validation is 39/39 including both n2048 cases. Full metric is 24222.796 us and n2048 is 114234.985 us versus parent near 23639/84027 us. Nsys measures one resident reducer launch at 93.606 ms per call versus parent reducers totaling about 58.1 ms per call, localizing the regression inside the fused progression rather than host launch overhead.

Narrowed the resident n2048 progression to exact width-8 panels so every update is one four-term TF32 WMMA K tile, removed the per-warp 16x16 shared scratch and strict scalar tail, and loaded/subtracted/stored accumulator fragments directly. Dynamic shared memory falls from 209 to about 137 KiB while all 372 former host launches remain collapsed. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric improves 24222.796 to 23808.331 us; n2048 improves 114234.985 to 90772.415 us, still roughly 6.7 ms above the selected parent near 84027 us.

Expanded the resident n2048 update from eight owner clusters to a cooperative 15-cluster/120-CTA grid, retaining the first eight clusters for exact panel formation and striping all full and fringe update tiles globally through grid barriers. Factors are consumed directly from the emitted [W,V,W] workspace with row-major/column-major WMMA views. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. The full metric is 23921.538 us and n2048 averages 98219.753 us, but 102 official target repeats span 84116.882 to 176600.769 us; the fastest run reaches parent territory while cross-grid scheduling variance makes the mean slower than the stable one-cluster-per-matrix 90772.415 us path.

Reduced the cooperative n2048 grid from the 15-cluster occupancy edge to 14 clusters/112 CTAs and passed batch explicitly so all eight matrices remain in the global update schedule. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric improves 23921.538 to 23808.780 us; n2048 mean improves 98219.753 to 92967.918 us over 108 repeats, with best 84278.130 and worst 140437.027 us. One cluster of residency headroom narrows but does not remove the cooperative timing distribution.

Reduced the cooperative n2048 grid from 14 to 12 clusters/96 CTAs with identical panel arithmetic, direct global factors, and grid barriers. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric regresses to 24044.207 us; n2048 averages 105003.704 us over 96 repeats with best 85524.925 and worst 177927.551 us. The measured 12/14/15-cluster points show 14 has the strongest mean, while every cooperative point retains a wide timing distribution absent from the original eight independent clusters.

Restored the stable one-cluster-per-matrix width-8 resident progression after the cooperative bracket, then repacked each remote rank's live V/W factors into contiguous 16x8 tiles with stride-16 WMMA loads; rank 0 retains exact source layout and fringe tiles read owner DSM. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric is 23895.143 us and n2048 is a stable 96853.022 us, regressing from the original resident width-8 layout at 23808.331/90772.415 us; transformed-copy traffic exceeds the reduced shared-bank cost.

Restored the original width-8 resident factor layout and computed only lower-triangular 16x16 WMMA update tiles, storing each accumulator to warp-local shared scratch and issuing coalesced direct plus transposed mirrored global updates so later panels still see a full symmetric matrix. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric regresses to 24021.397 us and n2048 to 103725.203 us versus 23808.331/90772.415 us for full-square WMMA; shared staging and mirrored scalar stores outweigh halving factor loads and MMA instructions.

Restored full-square width-8 resident WMMA, then suppressed the n2048-only global [W,V,W] triplet emission and removed its allocation by passing a null panel workspace; the full reflector matrix remains emitted for backtransform. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric improves from the original resident checkpoint 23808.331 to 23757.543 us and n2048 from 90772.415 to 90375.135 us; the roughly 0.4 ms target change is small but consistently removes unused O(n^2) traffic and allocation.

Widened the no-triplet width-8 resident n2048 CTA from 608 to 640 threads, increasing each matrix cluster from 152 to 160 update warps while retaining all arithmetic and storage. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric regresses 23757.543 to 24009.591 us and n2048 90375.135 to 103164.912 us; the extra warp plus stricter 640-thread launch bound crosses a large compiler/synchronization cost boundary instead of improving WMMA service.

Restored the selected 608-thread geometry and reduced each width-8 resident symmetric update from four residual-corrected TF32 WMMA terms to the two high-high products V*W^T and W*V^T. The strict n2048 refinement and exact certificate are unchanged. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39; standard n2048 scaled residuals rise modestly from about 3.22/2.72 to 3.37/3.13 but remain custom. Full metric is 23754.841 us and n2048 90244.535 us, statistically tied with the four-term no-triplet 23757.543/90375.135 us.

Kept one independent eight-CTA cluster per n2048 matrix but replaced per-rank DSM factor replication with direct row-major/column-major WMMA loads from the compact globally emitted [W,V,W] workspace; one-pass TF32 and full-square updates remain. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric improves 23754.841 to 23733.409 us and n2048 90244.535 to a stable 88097.893 us. L2-cached direct factors save about 2.15 ms versus shared replication and leave roughly 4.1 ms to the selected parent target.

Expanded the one-launch n2048 reducer to a non-cooperative 14-cluster persistent grid: eight owner clusters form exact width-8 panels, six helpers share all matrices' direct-global WMMA and fringe tiles, and a two-word device atomic barrier advances panel/update epochs. The existing info buffer supplies barrier state and is reset before eigensolve. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Full metric improves 23733.409 to 23648.420 us; n2048 improves 88097.893 to a stable 84987.930 us with only about 45 us range, nearly matching the selected parent aggregate while replacing 372 launches with one.

Raised the manual-epoch persistent n2048 grid from 14 to the measured B200 ceiling of 15 clusters/120 CTAs, leaving exact panel ownership, one-pass TF32 direct-global updates, and barrier semantics unchanged. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. N2048 improves from 84987.930 to a stable 84420.321 us with only about 53 us range. Full metric is 23648.698 us versus 23648.420 for 14 clusters because unrelated n1024/n512 samples move oppositely; target timing selects 15 clusters while aggregate remains noise-tied.

Removed the pre-sync from the panel-publish epoch because owner reducers already end synchronized and helper clusters have no writes, while retaining post-update synchronization and publication fences. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. Fast n2048 samples remain 84356.354 us, but 115 repeats average 87132.912 us with outliers to 164104.935 us; full metric regresses to 23712.013. The explicit first cluster sync is therefore required for stable all-rank residency at the 15-cluster ceiling.

Restored the required pre-sync on both epoch barriers while retaining the safe specialization that only the eight panel-owner clusters issue publication fences before the first barrier; all fifteen clusters still fence post-update writes. Build/kernelguard pass and validation is 39/39. N2048 is stable at 84355.161 us with about 100 us range, improving the fully fenced 15-cluster target 84420.321 us. Full metric improves to 23637.322 us, narrowly below the selected parent replay while preserving the single-launch progression.

Replaced repeated atomic read-modify-write epoch polling in the stable 15-cluster barrier with volatile global loads; epoch publication/count remain atomic and all pre/post synchronizations and fences stay intact. Build and kernelguard passed, validation 39/39. Full metric 23635.751030, n2048 84389.280 us versus trial 14 at 23637.321598/84355.161 us: target neutral within noise and aggregate slightly improved.

Removed the redundant device fence between last-arrival counter reset and atomic epoch publication. Every publishing leader still fences before its atomic arrival, the reset/publication remain device atomics, and cluster pre/post synchronization is unchanged. Build/kernelguard pass, validation 39/39. Full metric 23624.086946, n2048 84208.079 us versus trial 15 at 23635.751030/84389.280 us.

Shortened the volatile epoch-wait nanosleep from 64 to 32 cycles after removing the redundant release fence. Build/kernelguard pass, validation 39/39. Full metric 23632.157631, n2048 84154.938 us versus trial 16 at 23624.086946/84208.079 us: target improved 53 us but aggregate regressed 8.1 us, both near run noise.

Lengthened the resident epoch-wait nanosleep to 128 cycles as the opposite backoff bracket. Build/kernelguard pass, validation 39/39, but n2048 became unstable: 116 samples averaged 86440.999 us with 84.137 ms best and 163.331 ms worst; full metric regressed to 23695.772151. Rejecting the long backoff because delayed waiters amplify occasional epoch imbalance.

Restored 64-cycle volatile epoch polling after rejecting the unstable 128-cycle bracket and replayed the exact trial-16 source. Build/kernelguard pass, validation 39/39. Replay full metric 23639.217758, n2048 84179.535 us with only 7.3 us spread across three target runs; trial 16 of the identical source remains the best aggregate at 23624.086946/84208.079 us.

Completed 20 measured resident-reducer trials. Terminal commit a90bc70598dcf6f57dd17b16bc18aac5e4fdeb96 implements exact width-8 panels in one device-resident n2048 launch per matrix pair: eight owner clusters plus seven update helpers, direct global W/V factors, one-pass TF32 WMMA symmetric full-square trailing updates, and a 15-cluster atomic epoch barrier with volatile polling. It preserves reflector ownership, eigensolve/backtransform, certificates, fallbacks, guards, and all smaller routes. Kernelguard is clean and all 39 validation cases pass. Best identical-source aggregate was trial 16 at 23624.086946 with n2048 84208.079 us; terminal replay was 23639.217758 with n2048 84179.535 us and only 7.3 us target spread. Final nsys: two resident launches averaged 64.849 ms, 77.2% of captured GPU time. The fused path eliminates the former 372 host reducer launches but does not beat the old reducer compute time enough to materially lower n2048. Important deployment risk: the manual grid barrier assumes all 15 B200 clusters are concurrently resident, as established by profiling and repeated stable validation. Continue with concrete follow-ups: move the full-square update to tcgen05/TMA or a 2-SM cluster GEMM, reduce factor traffic by staging owner panels via DSM/multicast, pipeline panel formation against disjoint helper tiles, or replace the grid-wide epoch with a residency-safe cooperative launch once kernelguard-compatible APIs are available.

Replace the n2048 reducer's 372-launch direct-panel and GPU-wide baddbmm sequence with a device-resident multi-cluster progression: form exact wider panels, execute tensor-core symmetric trailing updates inside the extension, advance panel epochs without host dispatch, and retain reflector ownership, eigensolve/backtransform, certificates, fallbacks, all smaller-size routes, and CUDA guards; profile launch, reducer, and update phases.

Replaced the manual 15-cluster atomic epoch with cooperative clustered launch attributes and cooperative_groups grid.sync at both panel boundaries; CUDA now enforces full-grid residency at launch, eliminating partial-residency deadlock. Removed the barrier state argument and polling code. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full-batch benchmark completed 94 target samples without hang but was bimodal: n2048 mean 107798.021 us, best 83565.887, worst 169998.169; full metric 24124.245690. Nsys normal path: two resident launches averaged 64.361 ms, faster than terminal manual barrier profile 64.849 ms, indicating benchmark-level outliers rather than steady reducer slowdown.

Reduced the cooperative clustered grid from 15 to 14 clusters to leave residency headroom below the measured B200 ceiling while retaining formal cooperative grid synchronization. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full-batch target still showed the same bimodality over 88 samples, 114234.404 us mean, 84079.948 best, 169680.298 worst; full metric 24213.817833. Therefore the outlier mode is not caused by launching exactly at 15-cluster capacity.

Restored the 15-cluster cooperative grid and changed full-square updates to row-stationary two-warp-per-row work. Each warp retains TF32 row W/V fragments in registers while sweeping alternating column tiles, removing repeated row-factor global loads without shared-memory barriers. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 23965.225030; n2048 mean 99589.052 us over 101 samples, best 86243.217, worst 179373.993. The lower outlier-weighted mean versus trial20 came with a 2.68 ms slower normal best, measuring insufficient late-panel parallelism at two warps per row.

Raised row-stationary update workers from 2 to 8 per tile row, retaining each row W/V fragment across about 16 columns at the largest panel while increasing late-panel occupancy. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 24082.259410; n2048 mean 105667.930 us over 96 samples, best 83949.364, worst 175941.254. Normal best recovered 2.29 ms versus two workers but remained 0.38 ms behind the original cooperative tile schedule.

Raised row-stationary workers from 8 to 16 per tile row, retaining row W/V fragments for about eight columns at the largest panel and increasing late-panel occupancy. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 24458.873351; n2048 mean 130218.536 us over 77 samples, best 83348.656, worst 169110.901. The normal best improved 0.217 ms over the original cooperative tile schedule, while cooperative full-run outliers dominated the reported mean.

Pinned cooperative eight-block clusters to cudaClusterSchedulingPolicySpread while retaining 16 row workers. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 24500.226928; n2048 mean 132222.260 us over 76 samples, best 83312.721, worst 162251.144. Nsys showed the resident reducer itself improved to 64.083 ms average, but the same capture included thousands of cuSOLVER repair kernels; the slow mode is certificate-triggered fallback rather than reducer scheduling. Spread did not eliminate fallback incidence.

Added TF32 residual-correction MMAs to the cooperative 16-worker row-stationary update: high*low for V*W and low*high for W*V, reusing retained row fragments. This removed certificate-triggered cuSOLVER repairs. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39 with improved n2048 residuals. Full metric 23626.833182; n2048 stable 83423.668 us over three runs (83355.103-83461.533), 0.756 ms faster than the prior manual-barrier terminal replay. Nsys reducer averaged 64.175 ms with no fallback kernels, only 0.092 ms slower than one-pass despite two extra MMAs.

Raised corrected row-stationary workers from 16 to 32 per tile row, retaining each row W/V fragment across about four columns at the largest panel while doubling late-panel work supply. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric improved to 23620.002061, the best aggregate on this brief; n2048 remained repair-free and stable at 83498.708 us over three runs. Target was 75 us slower than 16 workers, within noise, while other active shapes produced the aggregate gain.

Implemented owner-panel DSM staging with one cooperative eight-CTA cluster per matrix. Each CTA stages 256 rows of the 24-float W/V record; WMMA and fringe updates access mapped remote shared pointers, eliminating repeated global factor reads. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 24362.817740; n2048 mean 122823.103 us over 82 samples, normal best 119587.120. Eight clusters did not provide enough update parallelism, so this measured the DSM traffic reduction with a 43% target slowdown versus the balanced 15-cluster global-factor schedule.

Restored 15 cooperative clusters and balanced DSM full-square work by partitioning flattened matrix row-workers into equal contiguous shards. Each cluster stages the one or two factor panels intersecting its shard across distributed shared memory; fringe remains globally balanced. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 24025.375544; n2048 stable 104074.384 us over three runs, improving 18.75 ms over one-cluster-per-matrix DSM but remaining 20.58 ms slower than global-factor row-stationary trial 27. This isolates remote shared WMMA/staging overhead despite restored parallelism.

First self-contained tcgen05 attempt: restored the global-factor cooperative baseline, added direct CCCL PTX wrappers for 64x16x8 TF32 MMA, per-CTA TMEM allocation, explicit SMEM descriptors and mbarrier completion, residual-corrected four-MMA accumulation, TMEM register epilogue, and scalar non-64-row coverage. NVCC rejected a deallocation block that patch context placed in an earlier finalizer (undefined warp/tmem_base at generated cuda.cu line 1131); the tcgen instruction code itself passed parsing to this point.

Moved TMEM relinquish/deallocation to the resident reducer epilogue and rebuilt the direct 64x16x8 tcgen05 path. CUDA C++ compiled the descriptors, mbarrier flow, MMA and TMEM epilogue, but ptxas failed on CCCL's unresolved architecture guard: tcgen05 allocation is supported only for sm_100a/sm_100f (and related family-specific targets), while the immutable harness uses generic -gencode sm_100. This records the fixed-build target incompatibility rather than a kernel source syntax error.

Returned to the verified cooperative global-factor path after the fixed sm_100 target blocked tcgen05, then raised corrected row-stationary workers from 32 to 64 per tile row (two-column fragment reuse). Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 23646.430932; n2048 stable 84058.192 us. This regressed target 0.559 ms and aggregate 26.429 us versus 32 workers, measuring excess repeated row-fragment loads once reuse falls to two columns.

Distributed each n2048 panel matvec over all resident clusters with cooperative grid barriers, global factor publication, and a grid-wide atomic correction dot; restored 32 update workers and added exact small-tail update. Correct 39/39 but synchronization and accumulator contention regressed n2048 to 301117.470 us and aggregate to 26102.871317.

Changed only n2048 exact-panel A*v reductions from four 8-lane subwarps to two 16-lane groups per warp, halving duplicate local reflector loads and improving transaction contiguity while retaining 304 row groups per owner cluster. Kernelguard clean and validation 39/39. Full metric 23622.955725 and n2048 83551.882 us: effectively tied with the 8-lane trial27 source (23620.002061/83498.708 us).

Changed n2048 exact-panel A*v reductions from 16-lane groups to one full warp per row, eliminating duplicate reflector loads and making matrix reads fully contiguous while retaining 152 concurrent rows per owner cluster. Kernelguard clean and validation 39/39. Full metric 23633.406419 and n2048 83528.366 us; target remains noise-tied but aggregate regresses versus 8/16-lane variants, so transaction width alone is not limiting.

Kept the original 8-lane n2048 panel row concurrency but interleaved each A*v dot across four independent accumulators to expose load/FMA ILP against the NCU scoreboard stall. Kernelguard clean and validation 39/39, with slightly lower validation residuals, but normal n2048 timing regressed to about 90.35 ms and occasional repair/outlier samples reached 146.24 ms; aggregate 23823.671779 and n2048 mean 92767.014 us. Reassociation and extra live state cost more than the latency it hides.

Corrected a source-attribution mistake: trials34/35 changed the legacy sytrd_panel_kernel, not the active resident reducer, so their target differences were noise. Restored that constant and changed the actual n2048 reduce_panel_clustered_body so each warp computes four rows together, reusing each reflector load across four coalesced matrix rows. Kernelguard clean, validation 39/39. Full metric 23659.336370 and n2048 84314.902 us, 0.816 ms slower than trial27; four live sums/reductions outweigh the reflector reuse.

Changed active n2048 panel matvec mapping from four rows per warp to two rows per 16-lane subgroup. Build and kernelguard passed, but validation hung on-GPU for 220 seconds and was terminated. Root cause is the full-warp shuffle mask used inside subgroup loops whose final iteration can diverge between the two half warps; every named lane did not participate. No benchmark metric.

Fixed trial38's subgroup deadlock by using __activemask() for 16-lane shuffles, then completed kernelguard and 39/39 validation. The two-row/half-warp panel matvec is nevertheless much slower and numerically repair-prone at benchmark batch8: full metric 25329.568232, n2048 mean 205987.492 us, best 103650.414 and worst 243993.668 us. Rejecting both the mapping and its altered reduction order.

Specialized the n2048 emitted factor record from [W,V,W] stride24 to [W,V] stride16 and updated the resident consumers, but patch context changed the n1024 host allocation instead of n2048. Build/kernelguard passed; validation stopped at n1024 with an expected [4,16] versus [4,32] batch-matrix dimension mismatch. No benchmark metric; allocation scope must be corrected.

Corrected trial40's host scope: n1024 retains its 48-float legacy workspace while n2048 allocates and consumes a compact [W,V] stride16 record, omitting the unused third W. Kernelguard clean and validation 39/39. Full metric 23649.053463 and n2048 stable 84016.688 us, regressing 0.518 ms versus trial27; the 64-byte pitch hurts mixed row/column WMMA access despite lower traffic.

Restored the proven 24-float factor pitch and allocation after stride16 regressed, but kept n2048 specialized to omit the third W store that the resident WMMA path never reads. Kernelguard clean and validation 39/39. Full metric 23618.512064 is the best aggregate on this brief; n2048 is stable at 83493.680 us, effectively identical to trial27, so the isolated traffic removal is safe and neutral-to-positive.

Combined the retained unused-W store elimination with a hybrid WMMA schedule: 16 workers per tile row above 1024 trailing rows, 32 below, capped by actual tile count late. Kernelguard clean and validation 39/39. Full metric 23628.336678 and n2048 83544.853 us, regressing 9.825 aggregate us and 51 target us versus trial42; dynamic mapping overhead offsets reuse/empty-phase savings.

Opted the resident n2048 reducer into nonportable 16-CTA clusters, assigning one 16-CTA owner cluster per matrix and 128 blocks at benchmark batch8. Build/kernelguard and all 39 validation cases passed because n2048 validation batch2 launches only four clusters, but benchmark batch8 failed at launch with cudaErrorCooperativeLaunchTooLarge (too many blocks). No metric; bracket cluster size below16.

Reduced the nonportable owner cluster from16 to14 CTAs, so benchmark batch8 requests112 cooperative blocks. Build/kernelguard and validation39/39 passed at smaller n2048 batch2, but batch8 still failed launch with too many blocks in cooperative launch. The nonportable packing limit is stricter than the portable 120-block grid; no metric.

Reduced the nonportable owner cluster to12 CTAs (96 cooperative blocks for benchmark batch8). Build/kernelguard and validation39/39 again passed at batch2, but batch8 still failed with too many blocks in cooperative launch. This confirms the B200 nonportable limit is simultaneous cluster placement count, so any >8 CTA cluster cannot host all eight required matrix owners in one cooperative grid.

Requested cudaFuncCachePreferL1 for the 137KiB-shared resident reducer to target the prior NCU L1 scoreboard stalls without changing arithmetic or scheduling. Kernelguard clean and validation39/39. Full metric 23638.107147 and n2048 83518.145 us versus trial42 23618.512064/83493.680; target is noise-tied and aggregate regresses, so retain default cache partition.

Removed the rejected L1 cache hint and changed the cooperative eight-CTA cluster scheduling preference from Spread to LoadBalancing, allowing B200 hardware placement to balance rank-zero DSM panel traffic and global updates. Kernelguard clean and validation39/39. Full metric 23614.357205 is a new brief best; n2048 83447.739 us improves 45.941 us over trial42 while retaining the unused-W store elimination.

Replayed the exact trial48 LoadBalancing source under a second full 13-shape benchmark as repeated full-batch stress. N2048 remained repair-free at 83484.212 us with 83438.126-83536.125 us range; aggregate 23621.778432 moved with unrelated shapes. Trial48 remains best aggregate 23614.357205; repeated target remains slightly ahead of trial42's 83493.680 us.

Combined LoadBalancing placement and unused-W store elimination with16 row workers instead of32. Kernelguard clean and validation39/39. N2048 improved to a stable 83432.844 us, the fastest continuation target point, but full metric regressed to23623.607430 versus trial48's23614.357205; aggregate objective rejects the change despite the small target gain.

Continuation completed through trial50. Terminal commit 56c002dc8 is source-identical to best trial48 ec7e35746 and implements a formally residency-safe 15-cluster cooperative n2048 reducer, residual-corrected four-MMA row-stationary updates with 32 workers, omitted unused third-W writes at the retained stride24 pitch, and B200 LoadBalancing cluster placement. Best full metric 23614.357205; source-identical stress replay 23621.778432. N2048 was stable/repair-free at 83447.739 us then 83484.212 us; 16-worker bracket reached 83432.844 us but lost aggregate. Final build/kernelguard pass and validation39/39 at terminal head. Final nsys: reducer 64.220 ms average over two launches, 77.1% captured time, no repair kernels. Important measured limits: grid-wide per-column helper panel matvec regressed to301 ms; DSM staging 104-123 ms; tcgen05 cannot assemble under immutable generic sm_100 (requires sm_100a/f); nonportable 12/14/16-CTA clusters pass batch2 but batch8 cooperative launches fail due cluster-placement capacity even at96 blocks; altered panel reduction order triggered severe slowdowns/repairs. No leaderboard submission was made by this worker.

Replace the n2048 reducer's 372-launch direct-panel and GPU-wide baddbmm sequence with a device-resident multi-cluster progression: form exact wider panels, execute tensor-core symmetric trailing updates inside the extension, advance panel epochs without host dispatch, and retain reflector ownership, eigensolve/backtransform, certificates, fallbacks, all smaller-size routes, and CUDA guards; profile launch, reducer, and update phases.

Re-measured 16 versus 32 compile-time row workers on both official n2048 correctness structures while preserving stride24, omitted third-W writes, four-MMA residual correction, LoadBalancing placement, cooperative residency and exact barriers. Three WPR32 repeats: dense batch2 67.703-67.730 ms, mixed 214.36-216.12 ms; three WPR16 repeats: dense 67.322-67.335 ms, mixed 198.87-209.46 ms. Both structures favor16, so no divergent optimum and no classifier/duplicate kernel is justified. Kernelguard clean, validation39/39. Full metric23640.790896; benchmark n2048 83439.568 us, target tied/slightly faster but aggregate regresses versus trial48, so this remains a measured bracket rather than selected head.

Restored accepted WPR32 and replaced scalar fringe factor-record reads with naturally aligned float4 loads for both 8-float W/V halves at retained stride24, preserving exact panel-column accumulation order. Cooperative launch/residency, LoadBalancing, omitted third-W write, four-MMA main update and barriers unchanged. Kernelguard clean, validation39/39. Full metric23635.342834; n2048 83311.366 us (83288-83349), 136 us faster than trial48 best target but aggregate remains 20.986 us slower due unrelated-shape motion. Retain for replay before selection.

Replayed exact trial52 aligned-fringe-load source. Full metric improves to23619.517571; n2048 repeats at83320.885 us (83260-83364). Across two runs the target is83311/83321 versus accepted source83448/83484, establishing a repeatable ~150 us n2048 gain. Aggregate remains 5.160 us behind trial48 due unrelated active-shape noise; carry the traffic reduction into further packing trials while retaining trial48 as aggregate best.

On top of aligned fringe loads, suppressed panel-workspace stores for rows inside the current factor panel and for terminal panels with trailing_size<=16; neither n1024 baddbmm nor n2048 resident updates read those records. Reflector output and retained stride24 consumer-visible records unchanged. Kernelguard clean, validation39/39. Full metric23645.584318 under noisy n512/n1024 outliers; n204883389.066 us, 68 us slower than aligned-load-only replays but still 59-95 us faster than accepted trial48/49. The tiny store reduction does not pay reliably; next pitch-preserving vector packing isolates store instruction cost.

Packed each consumed n2048 stride24 factor row into four aligned float4 stores, mapping consecutive lanes across W0/W1/V0/V1 segments while retaining the unused 8-float pitch tail and scalar n1024 triplets. Kernelguard clean, validation39/39. Full metric23617.997677 but n2048 regresses to83553.686 us versus83311/83321 for aligned-load-only and83389 with scalar unread-store suppression. Gathered shared loads plus 96-byte-pitched vector-store issue cost outweigh fewer instructions; reject packing.

Restored aligned-load-only traffic source and retained fixed WPR32 /32,%32 mapping, but after the uniform panel_start>=1536 threshold skip phases >=full_tiles before any factor fragment loads. This caps only truly empty late-panel workers without dynamic worker-count division/modulo or synchronization changes. Kernelguard clean, validation39/39. N2048 is83331.103 us, only10-20 us behind aligned-load-only repeats and still117-153 us ahead of accepted trial48/49; aggregate23670.287017 is invalidated by large unrelated n1024 mixed outliers. Exact cap is target-neutral, so bracket precomputed power-of-two thresholds next.

Replaced the exact full_tiles late cap with precomputed uniform panel thresholds at1792/1920/1984/2016, limiting fixed WPR32 phases to16/8/4/2 without changing /32 mapping or stride. Kernelguard clean, validation39/39, but benchmark n2048 became repair/outlier-prone: 106 repeats averaged94848.358 us, best83357.552 and worst185902.740. Full metric23889.011164. Although thresholds skip only mathematically empty phases, the changed compiled control flow perturbs the certificate margin; reject in favor of exact cap or no cap.

Restored source-exact aligned-fringe-load candidate after rejecting power thresholds. Fresh build/kernelguard and validation39/39 pass. Third full replay yields n204883316.065 us (83258-83370), matching prior83311/83321 and confirming a stable ~130-170 us improvement over accepted trial48/49. Aggregate23638.288947 again moves with unrelated shapes; aligned source aggregates across three runs23635.343/23619.518/23638.289, never beating trial48's23614.357. Keep trial48 as metric best, aligned candidate as robust n2048-local alternative.
